title: Quantitative economics
tagline: regressions, inequality, series and games, on this place's data
summary: The toolbox of quantitative economics on the place open: its tables of blocks, counters, wards and cells, the economies of the world, what is shown in the studio, or a table pasted. Every tool can run for each place, and its answers stand on the map and on the line of time.

tools.title: Questions of this place
tools.about: Questions put in plain words to the tables of the place open, answered by the toolbox and drawn on the map.

tools.title: Regression and panels
tools.about: Least squares, OLS, logit, probit, Poisson, PPML, fixed effects, random effects, Hausman, instrumental variables, 2SLS, difference in differences, convergence of incomes. Residuals on the map.

tools.title: Inequality and concentration
tools.about: Gini, Theil, Atkinson, Palma, Lorenz curve, poverty, Foster Greer Thorbecke, Herfindahl Hirschman, concentration ratios, location quotients, specialisation, dissimilarity, index numbers, Laspeyres, Paasche, Fisher, Törnqvist.

tools.title: Neighbours in space
tools.about: Moran's I, spatial autocorrelation, local Moran, LISA, hot spots, cold spots, clusters, outliers.

tools.title: Time series
tools.about: Autocorrelation, unit roots, Dickey Fuller, KPSS, ARIMA, forecasts, trend and cycle, Hodrick Prescott, vector autoregression, VAR, Granger, cointegration, Engle Granger, Johansen.

tools.title: Summary and correlation
tools.about: Means, spreads, quantiles, Pearson's and Spearman's correlations.

tools.title: Trade
tools.about: The gravity of trade, PPML, partner concentration, trade intensity, on the world's trade in goods.

tools.title: Growth and the short run
tools.about: The Solow model, golden rule, IS-LM, multipliers, growth accounting, total factor productivity.

tools.title: Games and choice
tools.about: Nash equilibria, dominance, zero-sum games, stable matching, Gale and Shapley, voting rules, plurality, Borda, runoff, Condorcet, Copeland, Schulze.

source: The methods: the foundations tyche and nomos and the economics domain, through the API's toolbox. The tables: the City of Melbourne's censuses and counters, Space2Stats, the World Bank, the OECD, and Freetown's flood assessment, as each table says.
